decisions.what: Anchor all .claude/scratchpads paths at the primary checkout (<main-repo> = first record of `git worktree list --porcelain`) instead of adding a copy-back step at worktree cleanup.
decisions.why: Copy-back cures the symptom only: artifacts are still lost if the worktree dies before the copy runs, and pre-fix artifacts did not merely vanish — they SPLIT across trees (subagent writes landed in the main repo via a cwd quirk while orchestrator writes landed in the worktree), so two divergent trees exist during every run. A single canonical write target eliminates both loss and divergence. The resolution technique was already prescribed by architecture.md §12 for session markers, and the deleted legacy /implement skill used realpath-anchoring for exactly this reason.
rejected: Copy-back step in /log-episode finale only: leaves artifacts stranded on session crash and keeps two divergent trees during the run.
Committing scratchpads to git: they are ephemeral working state by design; would pollute every feature branch.

decisions.what: Keep skill-logs (.claude/logs) session-local while scratchpads anchor to <main-repo> — a deliberate asymmetry, documented in architecture.md §8.3.
decisions.why: Skill-logs are written by the session itself and consumed in-session by auto-extract.sh, whose meta.json repo-field filter matches the session checkout; re-anchoring them would break that filter and move telemetry away from the session that owns it.

decisions.what: Migration for in-flight pre-fix runs: file-level, non-clobbering copy (worktree file copied only if missing at <main-repo>) in /log-episode step 1.
decisions.why: The original draft guarded on directory existence (copy only if the per-task dir exists ONLY in the worktree) — but pre-fix runs left the dir populated in BOTH trees, so the guard would never fire and worktree-only files would be silently dropped; a whole-directory copy conversely could clobber newer main-repo files with stale worktree snapshot copies. Caught by the behavioral lens of the adversarial review.

decisions.what: Retro-create ad-hoc WI GJS-34 and rename the branch to carry the code, rather than merging without an episode entry.
decisions.why: The episode schema requires task_id/plane_work_item_id and auto-extract.sh hard-requires a -GJS-<n> branch suffix; the fix was implemented manually in a chat session outside /implement-task, so neither existed. GJS-31 set the precedent for the adhoc feature-slug flow; merging silently (PR #54 precedent) would lose the reasoning trace for a contract-level pipeline change.
rejected: Hand-crafting the episode JSON without a real Plane WI: violates schema semantics.

blockers.what: GitHub branch rename closed PR #58 instead of retargeting it: the rename API retargets only PRs that use the renamed branch as BASE; a PR whose HEAD branch is renamed is auto-closed, and reopen fails once the old ref is gone.
blockers.resolution: Recreated as PR #59 from the renamed branch with the identical body plus a supersedes note; updated the Plane WI description and memory references.

blockers.what: SSH push failed (Permission denied publickey) — ssh-agent had no identities loaded.
blockers.resolution: ssh-add --apple-load-keychain (passphrase lives in Apple Keychain; prior user-memory note made this a one-command non-interactive fix).

dead_ends.tried: gh pr reopen 58 after the branch rename, expecting GitHub to have re-pointed the PR head to the new ref.
dead_ends.why_failed: GraphQL reopenPullRequest fails when the PR head ref no longer exists; head-side renames sever the association permanently.

learnings: Worktree scratchpad dirs are creation-time snapshots: every app-created worktree carried a frozen copy of .claude/scratchpads from the moment of creation (one worktree had 29 feature dirs all stamped with the same mtime). Any gitignored state referenced by relative path silently forks per-worktree.

Pre-fix artifacts did not just get lost — they split: subagent writes landed in the main repo (cwd quirk) while orchestrator writes landed in the worktree; one fix-cycle wrote different files to both trees. One-way copies are therefore unsafe; sync must be file-level non-clobbering union.

A mitigation can be silently lost when a skill is rewritten: legacy /implement passed SCRATCHPAD=$(realpath ...) precisely for this problem; its replacement /implement-task did not inherit it and no contract guarded the property. Invariants need a durable home in the contract docs, not just in skill prose — architecture.md §8.3 now declares the location contract.

Three-lens adversarial review (consistency / bash / behavior) found three different failure classes the tests missed: a relative path left in universal.md §7 (same loss class as the bug), the migration-guard flaw, and a pipefail/SIGPIPE hazard in `| head -n 1` under set -euo pipefail.
GitHub branch rename retargets only base-side PRs; head-side PRs close and cannot be reopened once the old ref is gone. When retro-adding a WI code to a branch, rename BEFORE opening the PR.
